fix_candidate.cause: Store.iter_operations (storage.py:831-833, bc738001) forces 'kv INDEXED BY operation_headers' with ORDER BY k. SQLite then sorts in a temporary B-tree, which spills to temporary files when the rows exceed its 2 MB cache. Each pending/notices envelope calls it in engine._pending (exclude_app='chrome') and Mail.unresolved_sent_checks (app='mail'), and every result builds that envelope twice.
fix_candidate.effect: mail_read and mail_search do 0 writes on main at any history; on the branch they create 6 temporary files and write about 5,400 pages per call at 1,000 retained operations (21,200 at 4,000). With every allocating write failing (ENOSPC), both return storage_limit from 700 retained operations; main answers them.
fix_candidate.not_in_ci: The sweep's fixtures hold only a handful of operations, so the sort stays in memory and the sweep cannot see it.
fix_candidate.options: Force the index only for selective state filters (states, legacy_open), or keep the primary-key order for app/exclude_app scans, or PRAGMA temp_store=MEMORY. Route to the builder; analysis changed no runtime code.
fix_candidate.safety_property: None. The index is a speed optimisation; for these two filters the forced index is no faster than the primary-key scan (14.3 vs 13.4 ms at 1,000; 56.0 vs 52.3 ms at 4,000; fulldisk-branch pending_scan_ms).
fix_candidate.title: Read-only Mail calls fail on a full disk once about 700 operations are retained
